title: First React learning workspace
goal: Create, understand, verify, build, and inspect a small Vite React learning project without treating the starter as a complete production architecture.
requirements: Create a Vite React project in the intended folder
Trace index.html to main.jsx to App.jsx
Replace starter content with a component hierarchy
Verify development updates and browser evidence
Inspect components with React DevTools when available
Create and preview a production build
Explain which production concerns remain outside this starter

steps.title: Check the environment
steps.task: In the intended parent folder, check the active Node and npm versions.
steps.check: The versions print in the same terminal, and Node satisfies the current Vite requirement.
steps.reason: The scaffold and build run in Node, so an unsupported or missing runtime must be fixed first.

steps.title: Create the React project
steps.task: Scaffold a named React template, enter it, and install its declared packages.
steps.code:
npm create vite@latest react-learning-lab -- --template react
cd react-learning-lab
npm install
steps.check: package.json, package-lock.json, index.html, and src exist in react-learning-lab.
steps.reason: The template creates a known starting structure and the install resolves its dependency graph.

steps.title: Trace the startup path
steps.task: Open index.html, src/main.jsx, and src/App.jsx. Write one sentence for the role of each.
steps.check: You can explain the path index.html → main.jsx → App.jsx without calling every file React.
steps.reason: Tracing the entry path makes blank-screen debugging much easier.

steps.title: Create a component hierarchy
steps.task: Replace the starter App with a page, header, and setup checklist.
steps.check: The page has one h1 and Components shows App with its two child components.
steps.reason: The small hierarchy connects component thinking to a real project without unrelated state logic.

steps.title: Verify development mode
steps.task: Start the dev server, open its printed URL, edit one list item, and inspect Console and Network.
steps.check: The edit appears, the document and source modules load, and Console has no unexplained error.
steps.reason: A visible update proves the editor, source, Vite server, plugin, browser, and React root are connected.

steps.title: Inspect React ownership
steps.task: Use React DevTools Components when available and compare it with browser Elements.
steps.check: Components shows App, Header, and SetupList; Elements shows their final DOM output.
steps.reason: The two panels answer different questions: React hierarchy versus browser DOM.

steps.title: Build and preview
steps.task: Stop the dev server, create dist, and serve the built output locally.
steps.code:
npm run build
npm run preview
steps.check: The build exits successfully and the preview URL displays the same useful content.
steps.reason: Development success does not prove that optimized assets and their paths work.

steps.title: Write the boundary note
steps.task: List what this project now provides and what a production product still needs.
steps.check: The note separates React UI, Vite tooling, and unresolved routing, data, backend, security, testing, and deployment decisions.
steps.reason: A working starter is the beginning of architecture, not the whole application.

acceptanceScenarios.when: The scaffold and install commands run in the intended folder
acceptanceScenarios.then: The project and lockfile are created without changing another repository
The browser shows the update and no unexplained Console error
App, Header, and SetupList appear as a hierarchy
The learning page renders from built assets

extensions: Move Header and SetupList into separate modules and preserve the same output.
Add one imported image and trace its development and build URL.
Write a decision record comparing this Vite SPA with one React framework for a specific product.
